newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai soybean ends little changed on uncertain.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai soybean ends little changed on uncertain.

text.p: Shanghai soybean futures ended little changed on Thursday due to uncertainties over the short-term market trend, traders said.
The key January 1997 contract ended at 3,190 yuan ($384) per tonne, losing 15 yuan. It opened at 3,190 and stayed at that level for the whole session.
March rose 23 to 3,238, May 40 to 3,350, July was unchanged at 3,350, September unchanged at 3,380 and November unchanged at 3,400.
Combined volume rose to 17,000 tonnes from 10,900.
Traders said most a lack of institutional speculation and poor sentiment made most investors stay on the sidelines.
"Trading remained dull with prices moving in a narrow range," one trader said.
"Prices were fairly static despite poor sentiment due to the lack of market-moving news," he added.
Analysts expect soybean to continue to move in a narrow range in the next few days.
